chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever visits his farm (property) and does not intend to stay for ten days, he shortens the prayer; and if he intends to stay for ten days, he completes the prayer."
ai.seo_question: When does a traveler start performing full prayers instead of shortened prayers according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the critical threshold of ten days for determining travel status (*musafir*) versus residency (*muqim*), a foundational concept in Shia jurisprudence for prayer shortening. It highlights that the intention (*niyyah*) of staying for ten days or more transforms the traveler into a resident, thereby requiring the performance of full (*tamm*) prayers rather than the shortened (*qasr*) ones.
